title: DPA Exception Rapid-Triage & Cross-Residency Prioritization Advisor
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Enterprise prospects and existing accounts increasingly submit ad-hoc DPA exceptions and cross-residency data residency requests that are slowing sales cycles and adding inconsistent triage overhead. We need a repeatable rapid-triage playbook and a prioritization advisor that classifies requests by legal friction, engineering lift, and business value so we can commit SLAs and routing lanes for Sales, Legal, and Engineering.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic scoring rubric (legal_risk, engineering_cost, revenue_tier) documented and approved by Legal/Eng/Sales
A lightweight intake form template for AE/SEs that produces prefilled routing metadata
Two automated routing lanes in the intake dashboard: 'Auto-Approve: Standard DPA', 'Escalate: Engineering Implementation Required'
SLA targets defined for each lane (e.g., 48h auto-review, 7d engineering estimate)
Integration points listed for Salesforce ticketing and Redwood Console intake view
proposed_flow: 1) AE files intake using DPA exception form -> 2) System runs scoring rubric and assigns lane -> 3) Legal reviews auto-approve candidates within 48h or flags for negotiation -> 4) Engineering is paged only for items with 'implementation_required' tag; product PM builds estimate and provides go/no-go within 7 days -> 5) Customer-facing comms template generated and tracked in intake ticket.
scoring_rubric: legal_risk: low|medium|high (factors: data type egress, required sub-processors, encryption expectations)
engineering_cost: trivial|minor|major (factors: network changes, regional replication, encryption at rest key management)
revenue_tier: P0|P1|P2 (derived from ARR bucket and strategic value)
notes: Design must avoid exposing PII in intake metadata; intake will store only redacted summaries visible to non-legal teams.
Target automation: reduce Engineering ticketing volume for DPA exceptions by 60% in Q2 after launch
Related legal precedent templates to be stored in Confluence and referenced by intake auto-suggest
timeline: Feb 14 - Mar 10: discovery & rubric workshop; Mar 11 - Mar 24: instrument intake form + dashboard views; Mar 25 - Apr 1: pilot with two AE teams and Legal; Apr 2 - Apr 30: iterate before full rollout
open_questions: What are the minimum data fields Legal needs to make an auto-approve decision?
Do we allow temporary geo-fencing (short-term routing) vs permanent residency changes?
How should we price engineering implementation work when required (one-off vs scope in contract)?
implementation_risks: Overly permissive auto-approve rules could create compliance exposure
Under-spec'd intake form will cause repeated back-and-forth and kill SLA targets
Engineering capacity constraints if many 'implementation_required' items surface concurrently
communication_plan: Pilot announcement to selected AE/SEs and Legal via email and Slack
Weekly sync during pilot with Legal and Eng leads
Playbook + FAQ published on Confluence and linked in Sales playbook
Train-the-trainer session for AE managers before rollout
